topic: Seatbelt Part 2: the vehicle sensor. What locks a seatbelt when the car brakes hard? (a weighted pendulum swings forward by inertia and tips its catch into the toothed lock wheel on the spool). Delivers the Part 2 promised in p052.
principle: When the car decelerates hard, the weighted pendulum under the spool keeps moving forward by inertia and swings forward on its pin, which tips the catch on its other end up into the lock wheel's teeth; when the occupant's body pulls the belt and the spool turns, the next steep tooth face hits the catch and the spool stops; when the belt goes slack the spool winds back, the tooth slope lifts the catch out and the pendulum hangs down again.

Part 2 of the seatbelt 🚗 What locks it when the car brakes hard?

firstComment:
Answer: a tiny pendulum 🔧

Under the spool hangs a small weighted pendulum on a pin. While you drive normally, it hangs straight down and the belt runs free.

Brake hard and the car slows down, but the pendulum's weight keeps going forward (inertia), so it swings forward. That tips the catch (the pawl) on its other end up into a toothed wheel on the spool.

Your body leans into the belt, the spool starts to turn, the next tooth hits the catch, and the spool can't turn. Locked.

Once the car has stopped and you sit back, the belt goes slack, the spool winds back a little, and the catch drops out.

US safety rules: this kind of retractor must lock before the belt pulls out 25 mm (1 inch) at 0.7 g, and it must not lock just because it's tilted 15° or less.

(Simplified 3D model, slowed down, with the catch on the pendulum itself, like the simplest design in the HowStuffWorks diagram.)

Sources:
HowStuffWorks, How Seat Belts Work (systems triggered by the car's movement; a weighted pendulum swings forward in a sudden stop; the pawl on its other end catches a toothed ratchet gear on the spool; when the webbing loosens the gear turns back and the pawl disengages): https://auto.howstuffworks.com/car-driving-safety/safety-regulatory-devices/seatbelt3.htm
US FMVSS 209, 49 CFR 571.209 S4.3(j) (emergency-locking retractor: lock before the webbing extends 25 mm at 0.7 g; if sensitive to vehicle acceleration, must not lock when rotated 15° or less): https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/49/571.209
altText: 3D animation of a seatbelt retractor seen from the side, with a dark belt wound on a spool and a silver toothed wheel on the spool's end. Below the wheel, a small pendulum hangs on a pin: a gold ball on a short rod, with an orange hooked catch on the other side of the pin. Light streaks pass in the background while the car drives. The car brakes hard, the camera jolts, and the gold ball swings forward, tipping the orange catch up into the teeth. The belt is pulled, the wheel turns until a tooth hits the catch, and it stops. Locked. The car stops, the belt goes slack, the wheel turns back, the catch drops out and the pendulum hangs down again as the car drives off. Text on screen: Brake hard. What locks? Brake! Pendulum swings forward. Catch into the teeth. Locked. Stopped. Belt goes slack. It lets go. Follow, new machine tomorrow.

It tips a pawl into the teeth. Locked.
